rationale: The active research path fixes one qualified economic executor/model and tests whether explicit decomposition/composition pays for its own overhead. Multi-model routing is not required by this track.
research_question: With the same frozen Luna executor binding and task corpus, does explicit task decomposition/composition improve verified solved-task economics relative to direct execution?

D0.name: LUNA_DIRECT_VERIFY
D0.policy: One Luna execution from the frozen task and exact audited base, followed by independent verifier.

D1.name: LUNA_PLAN_EXECUTE_VERIFY
D1.policy: One non-mutating Luna planning invocation emits only the frozen structured plan artifact; a fresh Luna execution starts from the exact audited base with the original task plus that plan; then independent verifier.

D2.name: LUNA_PLAN_STEPWISE_VERIFY
D2.policy: One non-mutating Luna planner emits the same structured plan artifact; plan steps are executed sequentially by fresh Luna invocations against one evolving candidate workspace; then independent verifier.

decision_rules: If D0 is not worse than D1/D2 on verified solve rate and has lower total-system cost, explicit decomposition is NO_BUILD.
If D1 improves the verified-success/cost frontier over D0, external structured planning earns further study.
If D2 does not materially improve over D1 after additional invocation overhead, stepwise decomposition/controller is NO_BUILD.
If gains are task-family-specific, later adaptive composition may be studied; no adaptive selector is authorized by this protocol.
If results are unstable or corpus power is inadequate, outcome is INCONCLUSIVE.
